¶ The Vermont independent has a point, as anyone who has watched the Terminator movies knows, but cooperation with the Chinese state would nonetheless not be in America’s interest.¶ Sanders is passionate about the issue. “What I don’t understand is how anyone can ignore when the world’s leading AI scientists tell us that, as AI becomes smarter than humans, it could operate independently of human control—with possible catastrophic results,” he wrote on X on April 30.¶ The day before at the U.S. Capitol, Sanders hosted American and Chinese scientists who advocated cooperation. “If President [Donald] Trump can sit down with [Chinese] President Xi [Jinping], I think leading scientists in America can sit down with leading scientists in China to discuss how in fact we can work together,” he told reporters.¶ Trump may discuss AI issues with Xi when they meet in Beijing this week. If so, this will not be the first time an American leader has tried to start a conversation on the topic.¶ President Joe Biden raised the issue of AI cooperation with Xi when the two leaders met in California in November 2023.

for the same reason.¶ There is no question that AI, as Sanders says, could pose an “existential threat,” but an agreement with China is not the answer as there is no evidence that Xi Jinping is more concerned about the fate of the human race than that of the Chinese he rules. So, perhaps he is more dangerous than the “craziest dictator.”¶ Is there any solution?¶ Perhaps the only one is to let Americans innovate, dominate AI and trust the good instincts of their tech community to develop sensible and humane standards. Such standards are unlikely to emerge from a world dominated by the researchers of a militant Chinese Communist Party.
